reviews.text:
Did I expect too much... So disappointed ㅠ.ㅜ

It was so impressive that Choi Hwa-jeong cried while eating Tongyeong vegetable bibimbap, saying it was a shame she couldn't bring her parents, and I was so happy that she succeeded after many attempts. but… It’s a delicious restaurant. He is a black and white chef. I had high expectations for this, and compared to that, I was very disappointed because the food was so unique.
But even if I went there without knowing it was a good restaurant, I don't think I would visit again.

1. The raw fish platter was so delicious and fresh, and the combination was great. This is my favorite.
2. The octopus mixed noodles with perilla seeds were too sweet and the overall taste was dry. In particular, the octopus seasoning was so sweet that I thought it was store-bought.
3. The first bite of the barley shrimp pancake was very savory and crispy, so I was satisfied, but it started to get greasy from the second bite.
4. The oyster bossam was okay. However, this level of taste was something you could get at any restaurant that specializes in oyster bossam.
5. Tongyeong Namul Bibimbap had a mild taste without red pepper paste. The style was smooth and smooth, which I like. But I was full so I left almost all of it.
6. The last melon that comes out is a melon, so I have nothing to say about it.

Maybe I expected too much… I ended up feeling really disappointed. ㅠ.ㅜ

I was so moved when Choi Hwa-jung ate the Tongyeong vegetable bibimbap and said she regretted not being able to bring her parents—she even teared up. That moment stuck with me, so after many attempts to get a reservation, I finally succeeded and was truly excited. But… because everyone kept calling it a “must-visit restaurant” and a “master chef,” my expectations went way too high, and the food just didn’t have much character in comparison. Even if I hadn’t known it was a famous place, I don’t think I’d go back.

Here’s what I tried:
1. Hweh platter — Absolutely delicious, fresh, and perfectly balanced. This was my favorite.
2. Perilla octopus bibim noodles — The octopus seasoning was too sweet, and the whole dish felt quite dry. The sweetness honestly made me wonder if the sauce was store-bought.
3. Dried baby shrimp pancake — The first bite was great—nutty and crispy—but by the second bite it started feeling a bit greasy.
4. Oyster bossam — Not bad at all, but it tasted like something you could get at any decent oyster bossam specialty place.
5. Tongyeong vegetable bibimbap — Very mild since it doesn’t use gochujang. The soup was also mild, which I usually like. But I was too full and ended up leaving most of it.
6. Melon dessert — It’s melon, so nothing much to say.

Gamta, octopus, salted perilla oil, capellini is a unique dish that can only be tasted here. The crispiness and savory taste of barley shrimp add to the barley shrimp water parsley pancake, and the taste is amplified by adding pickled onions. Cold meat made from pork front leg meat has a chewy texture and goes well with chamnamul and salted shrimp.
The highlight is the sea eel gomtang. It has a strong sancho flavor and is similar to loach stew, but has the clearness of jiri and the deep taste of eel. Strong soybean paste radish bibimbap made with pot rice signals the end of summer. The final dessert melon is soso.
Although he seems indifferent, he understands the customer's needs well and follows the speed of the customer's eating with a clean process. Completely satisfied with the service.

reviews.author: Because he’s a genius
reviews.text:
I went to this place because of its reputation as a black and white chef, so I thought, “Maybe it’s a concept restaurant,” but after actually experiencing it, I was more like, “There’s so much to see, but think twice.”
The price of the course is 58,000 won, which may seem expensive at first glance, but it is reasonable considering that it includes seafood, pancakes, stews, meals, and desserts.
The problem is that they are effectively selling wine and sake that start at 80,000 won per bottle, so when you pick up the bill, the price per person is well over 100,000 won.

Moreover, most of the customers are in their 20s and 30s and are addicted to Instagram gambling, so they are not interested in expensive drinks, and since they can't keep up with the drinks compared to the snacks, Diet Coke is flying around every table.
It's an interesting sight, but sake goes much better with this spicy dish than cola.

We started with seasonal seafood, giblet seaweed and seaweed wrap.
Croaker, abalone, cuttlefish, and shimesaba were served on one table. The croaker had zero fishy smell, and the abalone had no fishy smell even when topped with crab sauce.
In particular, Shimesaba took first place today as sashimi thanks to its ‘fishy aesthetic’.
The cutlassfish sauce, vinegar sauce, and sesame oil provided for dipping were all salty, making it ‘intoxicating’.

The capellini with gamtae and salted octopus that followed was the worst of the day.
The cold capellini texture becomes soft and the scent of salted octopus and perilla oil does not come out.
It's been a while since I left half of the noodles.

The barley shrimp, green onion, and water parsley pancakes are so delicious just from the smell of dried shrimp that they already pass the test in my mouth.
The warm shrimp tempura was crispy, but it was greasy due to the lack of oil.

The cold pork has a strong pork smell, so if you are the type of person who only eats the meat in sundae soup, you will probably turn your head.
However, if you add a piece of chamnamul and a drop of lime, it becomes a good side dish.

The highest point of the course is the sea eel gomtang with green tea leaves and Japanese pepper.
The strong scent of black pepper and Japanese pepper goes surprisingly well with the savory eel broth.
Thanks to the salty liver, it makes you want to drink water while eating it, but if you wash it down with a glass of alcohol, it becomes even more addictive.

The last soybean paste and young radish mixed pot rice is shown in its entirety and gives time to take pictures, but when mixing it, the sesame oil is so strong that it masks the taste of the soybean paste and young radish.
And as a Korean, it's a shame that it doesn't go well with sea eel gomtang.
The melon for dessert ripens amazingly and provides maximum satisfaction.

The staff service is friendly, but considering the two-hour limit, strong sales of wine, and additional corkage, “the structure is tight to enjoy alcohol properly.”
If your gathering involves drinking and chatting more than dining, we recommend that you carefully consider the price and time before making a reservation.
Although I acknowledge the charm of some of the dishes and the friendliness of the service, I doubt I will visit again as there are many options for the same price.

It looked small from the outside, so I was worried about whether there would be enough space, but they were operating with a plastic tent set up in the parking lot behind the store. It reminded me of when I was a poor college student and it felt like a nostalgic atmosphere.

Bottled beer and fried rice were brought to you before you even ordered. I was supposed to drink two bottles, but I ended up drinking one more because my aunt was so upset. I ordered grilled pollack and egg rolls, which are the representative menu items, and this grilled pollack is unique. It is not dry, but has a moist texture, as if it had been boiled and then baked. It's served with minced garlic that I'm not sure how to eat. I tried it with it on top and mixed it with soy sauce, but I couldn't find the right answer.

The French fries were freshly fried, some were long, and they were cooked well and crispy, which was perfect for my taste.

The price of the cocktail was around 8,000 to 9,000 won, which doesn't feel expensive, but it was about 1,000 won more expensive than other cocktail shops, so it didn't feel that expensive.

There were 3 dart machines, but I didn't use them so I'm not sure about the prices or anything like that.

I liked that the owner was friendly and spoke amiably to the customers. He made jokes and was polite to customers, but he did it at a level that never made me feel uncomfortable, so I felt good about it.

reviews.text: This is a large pub located in Mugyo-dong. They say it opened in 1971, so it's been over 50 years. They are currently operating many chains, including Yeouido, Yeonhui, and Mokdong, so you can find this restaurant even if you are not in Euljiro. The entire newly built, clean building is being operated as a pub. The first floor serves only bottled beer, and you can order draft beer on the second and third floors. They say the 4th floor is a rooftop concept, but I haven't been able to go up there yet. Because the surrounding area is a traditional office-dense area, there are many customers even on weekdays. The beers are all similar, but the main dish is seasoned whelk. It comes seasoned with whelk, dried fish, and green onions, and is spicy and delicious. The whelks are big and plentiful. The chicken is especially delicious, and has the feel of old-fashioned chicken. However, when I ate it this time, it was salty enough that I didn't need to add salt. The price has risen a lot, so if three people eat, it costs about 80,000 to 100,000 won.

reviews.text:
In Euljiro, golbaengi and green onion salad!

It's been a while since I had a meeting in Jongno, so after the meeting, my colleagues and I headed to Taeseong Golbaengi.
It's hard to eat a lot in the hot weather, so let's just have a light salad with green onions, noodles, and 2 glasses of 500cc beer per person!

In Euljiro, golbaengi is the truth. ^^

I think I've known this house for about 30 years.
There are a lot of places to eat in Euljiro and Jongno, but today, let's go to Taeseong Golbaengi...

Whenever we had a company meeting, this was always the second stop.
The office is in Gangnam, so why eat in Euljiro?
It's a place I've been frequenting since my business partners told me about it because I always went to work every day instead of on a business trip to Gangbuk.

I have fond memories of visiting with my wife a long time ago and having a delicious meal.
At one time, my wife loved this restaurant so much that she even made Euljiro Golbenggi at home on days when she drank beer at home.

It's been a while since I stopped by and the atmosphere has changed a lot, but the golbaengi is still delicious.

It was a bit early to have a drink, but after the coronavirus pandemic, it has become a trend for many people to go home early after an early drink, so it must be strange. ^^
Or maybe it's just me... lol

Anyway, I ate well and uploaded a picture.
